title: ～てくる — “go and come back / become / start to ～”
summary: Attaching くる to the te-form has several meanings: (1) go somewhere and come back, (2) a change that has been happening up to now, (3) a state or action beginning.

patterns.gloss: Verb te-form + くる (買ってくる)

body.p: 買ってくる (go and come back), 寒くなってくる (change), 雨が降ってくる (starts). The verb and context decide which.
てくる is change from the past toward now; ていく is change from now toward the future.

examples.ja: だんだん寒（さむ）くなってきました。
スーパーで牛乳（ぎゅうにゅう）を買（か）ってきます。
examples.romaji: Sūpā de gyūnyū o katte kimasu.
examples.tr: I'll go buy some milk at the supermarket and come back.

examples.ja: 空（そら）が暗（くら）くなって、雨（あめ）が降（ふ）ってきた。
examples.romaji: Sora ga kuraku natte, ame ga futte kita.
examples.tr: The sky got dark and it started to rain.

pitfalls: As an auxiliary, くる is normally written in kana.
Change-てくる is up to now; for the future use ていく.
